\section[il licenziamento]{il licenziamento — the dismissal, the sacking}

\label{lesson:IT-C357-licenziamento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the candidate, then the Italian for the hiring.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il licenziamento}
\textbf{il licenziamento} — \textquotedblleft{}the dismissal, the sacking\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Dopo il licenziamento ha aperto un ristorante.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{After being dismissed he opened a restaurant.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{licenziare} \textquotedblleft{}to dismiss\textquotedblright{}. \emph{La lettera di licenziamento} — the dismissal letter.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{licenziamento} is built on \emph{licenziare} \textquotedblleft{}to dismiss\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{licenza} \textquotedblleft{}leave, permission\textquotedblright{}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{licentia} \textquotedblleft{}freedom, permission\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{licēre} \textquotedblleft{}to be allowed\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il licenziamento}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the candidate, then the Italian for the hiring, then say \emph{il licenziamento} again

\section[dimettersi]{dimettersi — to resign}

\label{lesson:IT-C357-dimettersi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the hiring, then the Italian for the dismissal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: dimettersi}
\textbf{dimettersi} — \textquotedblleft{}to resign\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il direttore si è dimesso ieri.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The director resigned yesterday.}
\end{quote}

Reflexive, with \emph{essere}; past participle \emph{dimesso}. From a hospital, \emph{essere dimesso} is to be discharged.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dimettersi} comes from Latin \emph{dīmittere} \textquotedblleft{}to send away, to let go, to give up\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built from \emph{dis-} \textquotedblleft{}apart\textquotedblright{} and \emph{mittere} \textquotedblleft{}to send\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the hiring, then the Italian for the dismissal, then say \emph{dimettersi} again

\section[le dimissioni]{le dimissioni — the resignation}

\label{lesson:IT-C357-dimissioni}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the dismissal, then the Italian for to resign.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: le dimissioni}
\textbf{le dimissioni} — \textquotedblleft{}the resignation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ho dato le dimissioni perché lo stipendio era troppo basso.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I handed in my resignation because the pay was too low.}
\end{quote}

Always plural: \emph{dare le dimissioni} — to resign.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dimissioni} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{dīmissiō} \textquotedblleft{}a sending away, a discharge\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{dīmittere}, built on \emph{mittere} \textquotedblleft{}to send\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[disoccupato]{disoccupato — unemployed, out of work}

\label{lesson:IT-C357-disoccupato}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to resign, then the Italian for the resignation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: disoccupato}
\textbf{disoccupato} — \textquotedblleft{}unemployed, out of work\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Mio cugino è disoccupato da sei mesi.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My cousin has been out of work for six months.}
\end{quote}

Also a noun: \emph{i disoccupati} — the unemployed.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{disoccupato} is built from \emph{dis-} \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{} and \emph{occupato} \textquotedblleft{}busy, employed\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{occupātus}, past participle of \emph{occupāre} \textquotedblleft{}to seize, to fill\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{capere} \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[il preavviso]{il preavviso — the notice (period), the advance warning}

\label{lesson:IT-C357-preavviso}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the resignation, then the Italian for unemployed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il preavviso}
\textbf{il preavviso} — \textquotedblleft{}the notice (period), the advance warning\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Devo dare un mese di preavviso prima di andare via.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I have to give a month's notice before leaving.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Senza preavviso} — without warning.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{preavviso} is built from \emph{pre-} \textquotedblleft{}before\textquotedblright{} and \emph{avviso} \textquotedblleft{}notice\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{avvisare}, usually traced to Old French \emph{aviser} \textquotedblleft{}to perceive, to inform\textquotedblright{}, built on Late Latin \emph{vīsāre} \textquotedblleft{}to view, to behold\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from the family of \emph{vidēre} \textquotedblleft{}to see\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
